summary: This class explores Masekhet Arakhin daf 9, examining Mishnaic rules on minimum and maximum limits for full and deficient months in the Jewish calendar, as well as timing constraints for Shete HaLehem, Lehem HaPanim, and Brit Mila. It analyzes Talmudic debates between Rav Huna and Ulla regarding lunar calendar calculations, Rabbinic authority versus astronomical observation, and how leap years adjust year lengths. The Gemara also discusses the fixed year lengths according to Acherim, Shemuel's limits on a lunar year, and a story involving Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

questions: How many full thirty-day months can a lunar year contain?
Why are the Shete HaLehem loaves baked before Shavuot rather than on the holiday itself?
Under what circumstances can a baby's Brit Mila be delayed past the eighth day?
How do the Hakhamim balance astronomical realities with their judicial authority to establish Rosh Hodesh?
What is the minimum and maximum possible length of a lunar year according to Shemuel?
